title: Two municipalities hired us and then couldn't act on our findings because their IT staff didn't understand the remediation steps; we'd like a structured training programme we could sell alongside the audit, but writing curriculum and measuring knowledge retention is not something we know how to do.

record.text: Two municipalities hired us and then couldn't act on our findings because their IT staff didn't understand the remediation steps; we'd like a structured training programme we could sell alongside the audit, but writing curriculum and measuring knowledge retention is not something we know how to do.
record.detail: After finishing audits for two municipal clients, Opština Kanjiza and a second municipality we are not naming publicly, we delivered detailed reports and then watched nothing get fixed for three months. When we followed up, the honest answer from their IT coordinators was that the remediation steps read like a foreign language to them. We ran two informal afternoon sessions explaining the findings in plain terms, and that actually helped — one municipality patched four out of seven critical issues within a month afterward. So we know training works, but right now we deliver it informally and for free because we have no product to charge for. We would like to build a short structured programme — probably four to six modules — that we can sell as an add-on to any audit. The challenge is we do not know how to design curriculum properly, how to test whether people retained anything, or how to keep the material updated as the threat landscape changes. We have the technical content in our heads. We need help turning it into something repeatable and measurable. A good outcome would be a pilot programme we could test with one municipality client by the end of this year.
